cause.what_happened: HOST (the former Healthy Choice Wellness, renamed after a 2026-09-17 reverse merger into Host Digital Infrastructure, an AI data-center developer) fell 18.6% by 15:04 ET. Almost all of it came intraday, on 0.8x volume. There was no filing (the last one is 2026-09-24) and no company release (the last is 2026-09-22). It is the sixth session of a slide from the $8.00 offering price of 2026-09-17/18 to $5.00, on a thin tradable float, and it came on a day when AI and semiconductor names were weak and Oracle had issued a data-center force-majeure notice.

findings.finding: Issuer-side supply cannot arrive tonight. The 2026-09-17 underwriting carries a 45-day company lock-up (to about 2026-11-01) that expressly bars sales, including under the existing Cantor Controlled Equity Offering (ATM) agreement of 2026-08-26. The first holder lock-up tranche is not until 2026-10-17.
findings.mechanism_in_window: This is the window's forward supply calendar, and it is empty. The commonest second leg down for a microcap that just fell 18% on an effective S-3 with a live ATM is a draw that prints overnight, and the underwriting agreement contractually rules that out through 2026-09-29 unless Cantor waives it. It is dated by the lock-up terms rather than by an arrival.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on this line for HOST. The listed history is 3 sessions old, and the pre-2026-09-17 events in the baseline are Healthy Choice Wellness, a different business. The two post-listing drops went to -1.11% (after 09-18) and -18.57% (after 09-25, which is today), both in a window with the same lock-up in force. So an absence of issuer supply has not stopped this tape falling.
findings.why_not_priced: A thin, ATR-33% tape that has fallen 37% below its own offering price is trading as if more paper were coming. The filed terms say the issuer cannot bring it before about 2026-11-01, and holders cannot before 2026-10-17. If the price held this, the fall would sit on a disclosed seller or a news item, and neither exists. Instead it came on below-normal volume, which is the <2x profile the phase-0 table puts at +1.46% next session.
findings.independence: The 2026-08-27 8-K carries the ATM (Controlled Equity Offering) that the lock-up blocks: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1948864/000149315226040292/form8-k.htm. The Graham 13D restates the 30-day holder tranche date: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1948864/000095014226002581/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml. Both are the issuer's own filing family, so this is not a fully independent confirmation.

outside_window.finding: First 30-day holder lock-up tranche. For the Graham filers alone this is 4,497,355 shares, against a tradable float of a few million. The release is accelerated if the stock trades at 100%/200%/300% of the $8.00 offering price, which is not in reach at $5.

Resale shelf for the merger holders (Graham, Samra, Thomas, Monje): must be filed within 30 calendar days of the 2026-09-17 closing under the Registration Rights Agreement. It could file any day, but no date is set.
The issuer's 45-day lock-up ends and the Cantor ATM becomes drawable again. The company has a $391M-contract Site II acquisition to fund and has said nothing about how it will pay for it.
Site II definitive agreement. The company says it 'remains subject to negotiation', with no date and no stated consideration.
